title: Chapter 108: Finale
content:
Jakyeong narrowed his eyes, studying the open palm resting in his lap. An elderly Korean neighbor had once taught him the basics of palmistry, and he’d figured he would read Kang Il-hyun’s lines just for fun.

The man’s lifeline was ridiculously long—deep, unbroken, and stretching all the way down to his wrist. Jakyeong glanced down at his own hand; by comparison, his own lifeline stopped abruptly halfway down his palm, looking truncated and faint.

Il-hyun wasn’t looking at his hand at all; he was watching the play of expressions across Jakyeong’s face with quiet amusement.

"Well? What do you see?"

"You're sharp. And with a lifeline that long, you're going to live a painfully long life." Jakyeong held up his own hand for comparison. "Look at mine. It's cut short. People with hands like this don't usually last very long."

"What else?"

"Your personality is atrocious. Completely rotten to the core."

"Leave your personal grievances out of it."

"..."

"What about marriage lines?"

"You have one. Just one spouse."

"And you?"

Jakyeong spread his palm wide, a proud, teasing smirk playing on his lips. "I get two."

The warmth instantly vanished from Il-hyun’s eyes. Just as his jaw tightened to deliver a threat, Jakyeong’s phone chimed. It was an incoming video call from Wang Han.

Jakyeong held an index finger to his lips, shushing Il-hyun before accepting the connection.

Wang Han’s face filled the screen against a backdrop of brilliant tropical sky.

"Did you land safely?"

[Yeah, just finished unpacking. Where are you? Why is it so dark?]

Before Jakyeong could reply, a woman’s face leaned into the frame beside Han. Jakyeong blinked in surprise. It was Rita, the neighbor from their old apartment complex back in Kuala Lumpur. What is she doing in Thailand?

Rita waved enthusiastically at the camera.

[Wei! It's been forever! I heard you found a partner—Sasha was devastated when she found out, you know.]

The moment the name dropped, Jakyeong darted an anxious glance toward Il-hyun. Muting the volume, he scrambled off the porch and hurried toward the side yard. Il-hyun set his beer down, rose from the bench, and disappeared around the back of the house.

Jakyeong let out a quiet sigh of relief, only for Sasha to shove her way between Han and Rita, taking over the screen.

[Wei! I'll always be waiting for you! The second you dump that girl, come straight back to me!]

The trio burst into chaotic laughter over the speaker. Jakyeong offered a helpless, sheepish smile. He had already explained everything to Sasha months ago, and she seemed to have moved on, treating it as an inside joke.

After wishing Han a safe and relaxing trip, Jakyeong quickly ended the call.

Stepping back into the courtyard, Il-hyun was nowhere to be seen. Jakyeong settled back onto the wooden porch, looking around.

Heavy footsteps crunching over gravel broke the quiet.

Jakyeong turned—and nearly choked on his own breath.

Il-hyun was striding toward him with an unlit cigarette clamped between his teeth, holding a rusted, curved hand sickle in his right grip.

"Wh-What is that for?!"

Il-hyun crooked a finger, his voice dangerously smooth. "Come here. Lifelines are easy enough to carve anew."

Jakyeong shook his head frantically, backing away. "Are you insane?!"

Before he could bolt, Il-hyun seized his wrist in an iron hold. Jakyeong wrenched his arm back, driving a sharp kick into Il-hyun’s knee to break the grip.

Unfazed, Il-hyun tackled him onto the platform, pinning Jakyeong’s open palm flat against the wood. He raised the sickle and drove the curved blade down.

The steel tip slammed into the porch boards with a sharp thud, lodging dead-center in the gap between Jakyeong’s index and middle fingers.

Jakyeong shrieked, squeezing his eyes shut. When he opened them to find all ten fingers intact, he let out a shuddering gasp of relief.

You crazy bastard!

He shoved hard against Il-hyun’s chest, scrambling back to the far edge of the platform.

"Have you completely lost your mind?!"

"I told you to come here."

"What is wrong with you now?!"

"I made a mistake," Il-hyun drawled, leaning over the embedded blade. "Instead of tattooing my name across your waist, I should have carved it right into your forehead."

"Stop talking nonsense and put that damn blade away."

"Only if you say it."

"Say what?!"

"That you'll only like me for the rest of your life, and that you'll never sleep with anyone else."

When Jakyeong grimaced in pure disgust, Il-hyun rested his hand on the hilt of the sickle, nudging the blade toward him.

Jakyeong gave a reluctant, defeated nod.

"Say it out loud. Prove it."

Here we go again. Whenever his possessive streak flared up, there was no reasoning with him. Getting it over with was the fastest route to survival.

"I will only like Kang Il-hyun for the rest of my life, and I will only sleep with Kang Il-hyun," Jakyeong droned in a completely flat, robotic monotone.

Il-hyun’s brows arched in sharp disapproval. "Darling... there is zero sincerity in that delivery."

Jakyeong ground his molars together, putting every ounce of dramatic emphasis into the words:

"I will only like Kang Il-hyun for the rest of my life, and I will only sleep with Kang Il-hyun!"

Satisfied at last, Il-hyun pulled the sickle from the wood and tossed it into the dirt.

Jakyeong exhaled a long breath, muttering every curse he knew under his breath. When Il-hyun gestured for him to approach, Jakyeong stepped closer, only to see the man reaching for his smartphone.

Fearing the lunatic was about to replay an audio recording, Jakyeong snatched the device from his hands.

Instead of an audio player, the screen displayed a photo gallery. The images showed a secluded island—a lush, level expanse of land perfectly suited for off-grid living.

"What do you think? It's domestic, so travel time is minimal. You can hunt, fish, and live off the land to your heart's content. Acceptable?"

Scrolling through the aerial shots, Jakyeong nodded approvingly. "We don't even need a house. Pitching a tent is fine."

"Do whatever you like."

"I'll catch all our food, too."

"I thought we were planning a honeymoon, but it sounds like you're signing us up for survival training."

Hearing the grumbling, Jakyeong nudged his arm with an easy chuckle. It was hard to believe this was the same man who had been brandishing a sickle two minutes ago.

"Just remember one thing," Il-hyun murmured.

"What?"

"I still haven't rewritten my will."

Always a catch. Jakyeong gave a resigned nod. Fine. We'll be buried in the same hole.

Taking his beer, Jakyeong walked over to the low perimeter wall. Resting his forearms on the stone coping, the sparkling sea of Seoul’s nightscape stretched out below.

Il-hyun stepped up beside him, lighting his cigarette with a quiet, appreciative hum.

"Quite a view."

"I was thinking..." Jakyeong began softly.

Il-hyun turned his head, watching him.

"Instead of your estate... I wouldn't mind living here."

The words caught Il-hyun off guard; his expression stilled for a beat. Jakyeong waited quietly for a response.

He had grown fond of this place. The courtyard where he’d taken beatings as a boy, the dark shed where he’d hidden in suffocating silence—none of it carried terror anymore. Ever since Kang Il-hyun had handed him that bouquet of wildflowers, the house had ceased to feel like hell.

Il-hyun took a slow drag, exhaling a pale ribbon of smoke into the night. After a long silence, he gave a slow, deliberate nod.

"Let's do that."

Jakyeong turned to him in surprise. "Really?"

"I can simply come over every day after work, just like tonight."

"What's got into you? Agreeing to everything like this is actually terrifying."

"The one who loves more is always at a disadvantage," Il-hyun said smoothly. "What choice do I have? I have to cater to your whims."

He reached out, ruffling Jakyeong’s dark brown hair before leaning his weight in. Resting his head against Jakyeong’s shoulder, the tall, imposing corporate titan leaned on him with effortless trust.

When Il-hyun nuzzled his cheek into Jakyeong's collar like an affectionate hound, Jakyeong reached up, gently cupping the man's opposite cheek. Il-hyun smiled, a deep dimple indenting his jaw.

They stood side by side, taking in the glittering city lights before returning to the wooden platform to finish the beer. Lacking tolerance, the alcohol quickly made Jakyeong loose and uncharacteristically affectionate—a shift Il-hyun enjoyed so much he kept refilling the cups until Jakyeong passed out cold across the porch.

Il-hyun spent the quiet hours tracing the contours of the sleeping face beside him, only closing his own eyes when the eastern sky began to pale.
Chirping morning birds pulled Jakyeong back to consciousness.

He blinked against the daylight, his muscles stiff from sleeping on the wooden planks. Draped over his shoulders was Il-hyun’s tailored suit jacket.

Pushing the fabric aside, he heard Il-hyun’s low baritone speaking over the phone just outside the rusted gate. It was time to head back to the villa so the CEO could prepare for the corporate workday.

Jakyeong rubbed the sleep from his eyes—and froze, staring down at his left hand.

Drawn across his palm in permanent black ink was a bold, dark line, extending his short lifeline all the way down past his wrist.

He traced the ink with his thumb, a sudden, warm tightness catching in his throat before a quiet laugh broke past his lips.

The culprit was painfully obvious.

The rusted iron gate creaked open as Kang Il-hyun stepped back into the yard, his hair windswept and his collar casually parted. Catching Jakyeong awake, a brilliant, radiant smile spread across his face.

"Sleep well?"

Seeing the formidable executive looking so disheveled and fond made Jakyeong laugh out loud.

He held out both arms, and without a heartbeat of hesitation, Il-hyun crossed the yard and gathered him into a warm, unyielding embrace.
Autumn brought crisp, spotless blue skies over the city.

Outside the metropolitan community center, a long queue of local residents stretched down the block for a charity meal program. Stationed near the staging area, Reporter Yoon adjusted her telephoto lens, snapping continuous shutter bursts of Kang Il-hyun serving hot soup in a black volunteer apron.

"Something is off," Yoon muttered, squinting through the viewfinder.

Beside her, Senior Reporter Kwak snubbed out a cigarette. "What do you mean?"

"CEO Kang. He looks completely different."

"After surviving an abduction and losing his father, a man is bound to change."

Yoon shook her head. "That doesn't look like a man in mourning. He looks like a guy who just conquered the world."

"What about that new face beside him?" Kwak pointed toward the young man ladling rice at Il-hyun's side.

The youth was clearly neither corporate staff nor extended family. He worked with an easy, radiant smile, and every time Il-hyun turned to speak with him, the CEO’s usually frigid expression softened into an entirely different register.

"He's ridiculously handsome," Kwak mused. "An actor signed to their entertainment label, maybe?"

"Should we dig into his background?"

"Why bother?"

"Who knows? Maybe he's the hidden lever holding Kang Il-hyun's leash."

"Drop it. Let's just finish the PR piece."

Yoon refocused her lens on the young man, zooming in on his sharp, striking features. "Incredible..."

She pressed the shutter release.

At the sound, Il-hyun looked straight toward the press cluster. Yoon flinched, lowering her camera with a hurried, polite bow.

To their surprise, Il-hyun unclasped his apron and strode across the pavement toward the two reporters. Kwak stiffened nervously; the media team had approved the charity coverage, but having the conglomerate head approach them directly was unprecedented.

Reaching the reporters, Il-hyun held out two chilled bottled beverages.

"Thank you for your hard work today."

As they took the drinks with awkward bows, Il-hyun’s eyes drifted to Yoon's DSLR.

"Would it be possible to preview the shot you just captured?"

Finding no reason to decline, Yoon brought up the digital display. Il-hyun leaned in, reviewing the frame.

The image captured him and Lee Ja-kyeong standing side by side, locked in a moment of shared, unguarded laughter. A slow, thoroughly satisfied smile curved the corners of Il-hyun's lips.

Handing the camera back, Il-hyun offered a dazzling, model-ready smile.

"Could I ask you to send a high-resolution copy of that file to my personal office? I'd like to keep it."

"Ah... well..."

Kwak cut in smoothly, bowing. "Of course, President Kang. We will forward the raw file immediately."

Il-hyun offered a polite word of thanks before turning back toward the service line.

Left standing on the sidewalk, the two reporters let out a collective breath of relief, looking back down at the image on the LCD screen.

"Why would he want this specific photo...?" Kwak murmured.

"No idea."

They watched as Il-hyun returned to the serving station. The young man beside him reached behind Il-hyun's waist, carefully retying the apron strings with an easy smile. The subtle, effortless intimacy flowing between them was impossible to ignore—especially when Il-hyun leaned down, whispering something that made the boy laugh into his sleeve.

"Looking at the two of them..." Yoon started, tilting her head.

"They look like a married couple, don't they?" Kwak finished.

"Right...?"

"Surely not..."

Yoon shook her head with an incredulous chuckle, raising her camera once more.

Framed within the glass lens, the two men stood side by side beneath the clear autumn sky, looking for all the world like an exquisite, permanent masterpiece.

Whether they were spouses or not, they belonged together.

Translator's Notes (A/N):

  • Palmistry & Life Lines (손금 & 생명선): In East Asian palmistry, a deep, continuous line wrapping around the base of the thumb (lifeline) signifies vitality and longevity, while a broken or short line traditionally forebodes a premature death. Il-hyun drawing a pen stroke to extend Jakyeong's lifeline reflects his obsessive determination to keep the former assassin alive by his side indefinitely.

  • Chaebol Corporate Philanthropy (기업 사회공헌 & 급식 봉사): High-profile Korean conglomerates frequently conduct public volunteer work—such as soup kitchen service (geupshik bongsa)—following legal controversies or executive successions to rehabilitate public relations and project humility before the press.
